Key artifacts

Specification

Move the ledger and payouts tables from MySQL 5.7 to Postgres 16 using a dual-write window of 7 days, then cut reads over per service.

Implementation Plan

4 task groups: schema port, dual-write adapter, backfill job, read cutover. Backfill runs off-peak in 50k-row batches.

Decisions

specification

  • Dual-write for 7 days — lets us compare row counts before any read moves
  • Keep MySQL read-only for 30 days after cutover — rollback without data loss

gap_analysis

  • Replace ENUM columns with lookup tables — Postgres enums are costly to alter

Risks

  • Open — Backfill may exceed the nightly window for the 2019–2021 ledger partitions
  • Open — Two reporting services read MySQL directly and are not in the cutover plan
  • Timezone handling differs for DATETIME columns Resolved

Raw state

mockups.title: Artifact Reader Implementation Plan
mockups.html:
payments-platform — Visual Studio Code
⎘⌕⑂◈2✳
✳ Claude Code
◈ Maister · Implementation Plan
Skip to document
← Auth token rotation › Implementation Plan
TL;DR

Four task groups replace long-lived refresh tokens with single-use rotating tokens. Storage change first, then the rotation job, reuse detection and client SDK updates. Existing sessions migrate lazily on next refresh.

Key decisions
  • Rotate on every use — limits replay to one request
  • Reuse revokes the whole family — standard theft response
Open questions & risks
  • Mobile clients on v3.x can't handle a rotated token
  • Clock skew on token expiry Resolved
Checklist: 14 of 22 done · 1 skipped

Task Group 1: Token storage

  • ☑ 1.1 Add token_family_id and rotated_at columns
  • ☑ 1.2 Write migration with backfill for active sessions
  • ☑ 1.3 Tests: family lookup, expiry index

Task Group 2: Rotation job

  • ☑ 2.1 Issue a new refresh token on every /token/refresh
  • ☑ 2.2 Invalidate the previous token atomically
  • ☐ 2.3 Grace window of 10 s for concurrent refreshes
  • ⊘ 2.4 Redis cache for token lookups (skipped: p95 already under 5 ms)

Task Group 3: Reuse detection

  • ☐ 3.1 Detect reuse of a rotated token and revoke the family
